messages.content: What is the change in entropy in Joules per Kelvin of a 1kg ice block at 0°C if it is heated to 100°C under 1 atmosphere of pressure?

function.name: entropy_change_calculate
function.description: Calculate the change in entropy for a mass of a specific substance under set initial and final conditions. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

substance.description: The substance for which the change in entropy is calculated.

mass.description: The mass of the substance in kg.

initial_temperature.description: The initial temperature of the substance in degree Celsius.

final_temperature.description: The final temperature of the substance in degree Celsius.

pressure.description: The pressure the substance is under in atmospheres.

But the process includes phase change: ice at 0°C to water at 0°C (melting), then water from 0°C to 100°C, then water to steam at 100°C (boiling). But the question says "ice block at 0°C heated to 100°C under 1 atm". That implies melting and boiling. So we need to compute ΔS = ∫ dQ_rev/T. For each stage: melting at 0°C: ΔS_melt = m * L_f / T_m (T in K). L_f = latent heat of fusion of water ~ 334 kJ/kg. T_m = 273.15 K. So ΔS_melt = 1 kg * 334000 J/kg / 273.15 K = about 1222 J/K.

Then heating water from 0°C to 100°C: ΔS_water = m * ∫ c_p_water dT / T. For water, specific heat ~ 4184 J/(kg·K). So ΔS_water = m * c_p * ln(T_final/T_initial) = 1 kg * 4184 J/kg/K * ln(373.15/273.15). ln(373.15/273.15)=ln(1.366)=0.312. So ΔS_water ≈ 4184 * 0.312 = 1305 J/K.

Then boiling at 100°C: ΔS_boiling = m * L_v / T_b. L_v = latent heat of vaporization ~ 2260 kJ/kg. T_b = 373.15 K. So ΔS_boiling = 2260000 J/kg / 373.15 K = 6060 J/K.

Total ΔS = 1222 + 1305 + 6060 = 8587 J/K. Roughly 8600 J/K.
